missing: Dose cell has no track for rodent/cynomolgus GLP toxicology (rodent-nhp-glp-tox), which stated NOAEL AUC margins for eteplirsen (20x monkey, 6x juvenile rat; 206488 PharmR) and a small margin for golodirsen (211970 PharmR). Patients were dosed at 30 mg/kg without renal toxicity, so this is a candidate dose 'same' with margin_stated true, provided the margin was stated before dosing.

Vesleteplirsen (member, PPMO): MOMENTUM stopped for persistent hypomagnesemia and declining kidney function (Sarepta community letter 'Update SRP-5051 Program', 2024; AJMC 'Sarepta Halts Development'). Its nonclinical renal and electrolyte predictions were not found. The safety cell should carry it at least as an unsettled/unpublished note, and checking for a public nonclinical source is worthwhile, because this patient renal harm cuts against the 'kidney toxicity absent in patients' contra.

hDMD transgenic mouse (full human DMD locus), used in Arechavala-Gomeza 2007 (doi:10.1089/hum.2006.061) to pick the human exon 51 sequence. It is a separate system from patient myoblasts and could be its own engagement track.

PRO044 and PRO045 (members, 2'OMePS): patient exon-skipping and dystrophin data exist (PRO044 NCT01037309; PRO045 NCT01826474), and BioMarin discontinued them in 2016. The draft has no entry for these members; engagement pairings were not verified here.
Cynomolgus monkey exon 53 skipping for viltolarsen (Watanabe 2018, doi:10.1016/j.omtn.2018.09.017) is a possible further engagement track; not verified in full text.
rule_questions: mdx efficacy contra (2024): in mdx, function improved only above about 10% dystrophin (Wu 2011: none at 2.6%), and patients reached about 1-6%. Is RACER53/ESSENCE a contra, or a result under conditions the model never tested (untested)? The trial sources do not cite dystrophin level as the cause (NS Pharma cites age, duration and steroids), so contra stands under the literal rule.
ESSENCE (listed in patient_trials) pooled golodirsen with casimersen, which is not in the class member list. Is a pooled primary admissible as a patient datum for the member drug?

Eteplirsen's GLP tox gave kidney NOAEL margins that held in patients. Does that belong in safety (2016 'same' before golodirsen's 2019 contra) or only in dose under Decision 16? The brief's 'count the harm once' does not settle it when the harm never appeared.

Do the class members' renal-monitoring label warnings, plus vesleteplirsen's patient kidney decline on the same PMO backbone with a peptide, make the 'renal toxicity absent' contra 'other' (same platform showed the harm), or is PPMO a different platform?
